chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Muthanna ibn al-Walid al-Hannat, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Do not enter the bathhouse unless there is something in your stomach to extinguish the heat of the stomach with, and it is stronger for the body, and do not enter it while you are filled with food.
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended state of the stomach when entering a bathhouse according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) prescribes entering the bathhouse with a moderate amount of food to mitigate the 'heat of the stomach,' reflecting the contemporary medical understanding of humoral balance and bodily strength. This ruling balances the physical benefits of bathing with digestive health, advising against both empty-stomach vulnerability and the lethargy of overeating. The guidance underscores the Shia emphasis on maintaining physical well-being as a prerequisite for spiritual devotion.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Al Musna Bin Al Waleed Al Hannat, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Do not enter the bathhouse except in your inside is something to cool down the heat of your stomach with, and it is more strengthening for your body, and do not enter it and you are filled up from the food’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ahmad ibn Muhammad has narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam from al-Muthanna’ al-Hannat from abu Basir who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Do not enter a bathhouse until there is something in your belly to calm down the excitement of your stomach and it is more energizing for the body. Do not enter it with your stomach full of food.’”
